policy.green_round_definition: Five explicit workflow_dispatch runs on the same frozen branch and head: CI, cluster-e2e with suite=all, docker-e2e, chain-semantics-e2e, and cluster-validate. Every existing chaos shard and both stages must be green. Failure, cancellation, or missing coverage resets the streak. Incomplete rounds do not advance it; partial reruns cannot replace complete rounds.

failures.observed: Blank member 0 reaches block 510 after 20s. Its colocated executor then stalls at block 523 while the surviving fleet reaches block 640; convergence fails with lag 117. Executor logs show exec_txs recordings time out after the wipe.
failures.cause: The case removes archive/dir, which belongs to the shared Aeron driver and records the live executor. The fault is intended to remove only member data.
failures.change: Share the fleet wipe operation with the member rejoin case. Preserve archive/dir, remove hidden member files as well as ordinary files, and test the operation on a temporary tree.
failures.status: Harness scope corrected; PR 839 still reproduces the stall because peer seeding also recursively deletes the nested archive.
verification: Temporary-tree wipe test verifies member data is removed, including hidden files, while live archive/dir, executor state, and egress files survive.

failures.observed: An aggregate increase of three rebuild lines can come entirely from one mirror. The mirror-kill case previously required only one rebuild.
failures.change: Require an increased log count from each node and allocation; a replacement allocation needs its own completed rebuild. Report missing nodes on timeout.
verification: Unit tests reject repeated rebuilds on one mirror, missing or regressed evidence, and replacement allocations without their own completed rebuild.

failures.observed: A 404 for a live allocation is interpreted as an empty clean log, so the divergence scan can pass without evidence.
failures.change: Try the node agent and retry missing live logs. Preserve empty-log behavior for terminal allocations.
verification: Fake-agent tests verify live 404 fallback, live missing-log failure, and terminal 404 compatibility.

failures.observed: With a live Redis head at position 10 and local progress 100 beyond max_stale_txs=8, cold nonce/balance RPCs return (3,0) while the executor returns (5,42).
failures.cause: Account RPCs share the admission cache lookup without requiring Redis freshness. A lower bound is suitable for nonce admission, but a known-stale row must not answer a head-state RPC.
failures.change: Require freshness for the RPC specialization of the cache read. Keep the admission specialization independent of freshness and executor queries. Local resident rows retain priority.
failures.hot_path_detail: The shared async helper has a const REQUIRE_FRESH parameter. RPC instantiates true; admission instantiates false, eliminating the new condition and head loads from admission. Healthy cold RPC adds the freshness check; stale cold RPC uses the existing bounded executor query.
failures.status: fix validated locally; full CI and full workload comparison pending
verification: A real Redis regression fails with (3,0), then passes with (5,42).
Fresh Redis and local reads make zero executor queries.
Validated admission uses stale nonce lower bounds and makes zero executor queries.
Five release repeats per version, 400 samples per phase: fresh RPC p99 221.81 -> 205.52 us; serial admission median 3282.38 -> 3988.67 TPS. Shared-host variation prevents a speedup claim.
Performance summary and raw samples: docs/benches/2026-10-26-ingress-rpc-cache-profile.json

failures.observed: A peer accepts request headers and never answers. Closing the source, replacing the request, or dropping the reader leaves each old HTTP request alive. All three cancellation regressions fail before the fix.
failures.cause: EgressTransport discards the spawned replay JoinHandle. Dropping the output receiver does not cancel the HTTP task, and the request has no deadline. Reader resends can leave more abandoned workers.
failures.change: Make Replay own its worker and abort it on replacement, close, or drop. Bound each page request, including its body, to five seconds.
failures.hot_path_detail: Only replay setup, teardown, and HTTP reads change. Polling still reads the same receiver. Admission and execution add no work. Full deployed workload comparison remains pending.
failures.reason_missed: Existing egress tests use an answering local peer or a refused connection. They do not hold a connection open without a response or check abandoned requests.
failures.status: All 209 engine library tests pass, including five real-socket cancellation and deadline regressions. This independently reproduced bug is not established as the cause of the validator CI stall.
verification: Before-fix failure: /tmp/chaos-gaps-replay-cancel-before.log

failures.observed: Two configured providers accept HTTP calls but send no reply. finalized_block_number remains pending past 35 seconds; the follower has no returned error to raise its halt or rotate the sources.
failures.cause: The set joins all provider reads without a deadline. The default HTTP transport has no configured request timeout. An established but silent connection differs from an immediate HTTP refusal.
failures.change: Bound each member read, including light-client reads and all log/header methods, to 30 seconds. Timeout becomes a provider error and uses the existing source rotation, halt, and backoff rules. HTTP and WebSocket selection stays unchanged.
failures.hot_path_detail: The L1 read path adds a deadline per source operation. It changes failure timing. Admission and execution add no work. Full deployed workload comparison remains pending.
failures.reason_missed: Scripted source mocks return answers or errors. Earlier transport faults answer 503/429 immediately. No case holds every provider connection open without a response.
failures.status: Real HTTP regression fails before the deadline, then passes with source-out halt, no requests during backoff, and automatic recovery. Full CI pending.
verification: Before: /tmp/chaos-gaps-l1-deadline-before.log (35-second bound expires).
After: /tmp/chaos-gaps-l1-deadline-after.log (3 tests pass, including deadline/backoff/recovery).
